title: Draupadi's swayamvara
hook: two brothers come home with a princess, and their mother answers without looking

segments.voice: Yesterday: the disguised archer bowed, strung the bow, and the mark fell. Your line was the mark falls to the ground.

Someone in the crowd has worked it out. While the kings fight, Krishna watches the brahmin with the bow and the giant with the tree, and turns to his brother Balarama. That one with the tree, he says, is Bhima. The archer is Arjuna. They didn't die in the fire. Meanwhile, at the potter's house where the family is staying, Kunti waits. It's late, and her sons haven't come back.

Bhima and Arjuna come to the door with Draupadi. They're living as brahmins, on alms, so they call in: look, we've brought alms. And Kunti, inside, without looking up, answers the way a mother might: share it, all of you. Then she sees who's standing there. A princess, not a bowl of rice. What have I said, Kunti cries, the text says. She can't simply take back her word, and she won't let it be false. So she takes Draupadi by the hand, goes to Yudhishthira, and asks how her word can stay true without wrong being done to the princess. Yudhishthira turns first to Arjuna: you won her, she's yours. Arjuna won't hear of it; the eldest should marry first. Then Yudhishthira sees all his brothers looking at Draupadi. He remembers words Vyasa once spoke, and fears the brothers could be divided over her if only one marries her. So he says she'll be the wife of all. A word said without looking. It happens in families: the yes called from the other room. What stands out isn't the slip. It's that Kunti treats her own word as weighty enough to need care, even when she didn't mean it. And then Krishna arrives at the potter's door with Balarama, and bows at Yudhishthira's feet. The cousins meet face to face.
screen: `WE'VE BROUGHT ALMS.` · `SHARE IT, ALL OF YOU.` · `WHAT HAVE I SAID?` · `KRISHNA AT THE DOOR.`

segments.voice: Bring back something you said this week without really looking: a quick yes, a careless answer, a word from the other room. Breathe in and see it clearly; breathe out and let it rest where you can find it later. If there's something to mend, it can wait.
Draupadi's swayamvara. Today, the homecoming: alms announced at the door, a mother's answer given without looking, and Krishna arriving.
Your line: share it, all of you. A word said without looking still mattered to Kunti. Day seven hundred forty-four, done.

howItsDone: Bhiksha, food given as alms, is part of Hindu religious life: renunciants, and in some traditions students, receive food from householders, which is why the brothers, dressed as brahmins, call what they bring home alms.

chat.says: Why did Kunti say 'share it, all of you' about Draupadi?

chat.meaning: Hearing 'we've brought alms,' Kunti said share it without looking. Seeing a princess, she cried 'what have I said?' but wouldn't let her word be false.

Kunti.meaning: mother of the Pandavas, who answers without looking

Vyasa.meaning: the sage held to have composed the Mahabharata

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Swayamvara Parva (Krishna recognizes the Pandavas; the return to the potter's house; Kunti's words; Yudhishthira's decision; Krishna and Balarama visit)

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm in Ganguli: Krishna identifies Bhima and Arjuna to Balarama during the fight; the family lodges at a potter's house; Kunti answers 'enjoy/share ye all' without looking, then cries 'what have I said?'.

Confirm the sequence: Yudhishthira first offers Draupadi to Arjuna, Arjuna refuses in favor of the eldest, then Yudhishthira sees all the brothers looking at her, recalls Vyasa's words and fears division.
Confirm Krishna 'bows at Yudhishthira's feet' on arriving at the potter's house.
Dhrishtadyumna secretly following the brothers home is omitted.

Editor pass: Yudhishthira's fear is of division among the brothers (as the notes and trapdoor say), not of what Draupadi 'could do' to them; reworded to avoid casting her as the danger. Cut the general claim that brahmins live on alms.
